To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the global burden of disease is not a major factor in the production of global medical knowledge.

the production of research on health conditions is strongly influenced by local disease burden, and that this local disease burden is strongly influenced by the wealth of the country where the research is conducted.
global disease burden is inversely correlated with the production of health research relevant to that disease burden.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of health research and its relevance to global health needs.
how global health inequality affects the production of medical knowledge.
the global inequality of health knowledge, a topic neglected in global health research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a global disparity of health research that is likely to be a consequence of the global disparity in wealth.

there is an inverse relationship between the burden of a disease in a country and the amount of research conducted in the country, which is not necessarily related to the amount of research in the world.
the health needs of less developed countries are not being addressed by the research infrastructure of developed countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the health research community is not paying sufficient attention to the global burden of disease.
the health research system is biased against health problems in the world's poor.
the global burden of health research is grossly unequal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the global health research enterprise is not adequately addressing the global health burden.
the global disparity in the production of research on diseases and conditions is not simply a reflection of the disparity in wealth or in disease burden.
the global disparity of research production is driven by the global distribution of disease burden and the local distribution of research capacity.
